title: Scrappy Video Understanding
label: Scrappy Video Understanding, a skill for any assistant
creator: Danny
creatorRole: who teaches the course Astrolabe came out of
promise: Scrappy multi-pass video understanding: takes any video link or file, grabs keyframes and contact sheets, extracts subtitles/audio, and analyzes scenes.

hero.alt: A video timeline with contact sheet, extracted frames, subtitle text, and an understanding summary card

changes.note: Starts from the file on disk, asks before sending a video anywhere, handles private GitHub links, and writes a phone-friendly report.html.
Private GitHub links get a folder named after the file, and report.html now carries its contact sheet inside it.

desc: Free. Resourceful and efficient video understanding without fragile setups or heavy GPU requirements. Tries the fastest, leanest pass first: instant subtitle harvesting via yt-dlp with zero video download, rapid metadata probe, and single-glance 4x3 contact sheets, escalating to deep scene-cut extraction only where needed. Accepts YouTube, X/Twitter, TikTok, Loom, Vimeo, direct web links, or local video/audio files. Built on yt-dlp (Unlicense) and ffmpeg (LGPL/GPL).
bio: Danny teaches the course Astrolabe came out of. He built this for quick, versatile video analysis across any platform or local recording.

steps: add the Scrappy Video Understanding skill to your notes folder, so every assistant has it
if Claude Code is here, also add the plugin marketplace goggledefogger/skills-town, turn on auto-update for it and install scrappy-video-understanding
pin the Scrappy Video button to your Astrolabe chat ribbon
install.updates: Auto-updates once that marketplace has it switched on; on any other agent, npx skills update brings the next version.
install.touches: Adds the skill to your notes folder's skills, plus the Claude Code plugin if Claude Code is here, and a card to your Astrolabe rituals shelf. Adds ffmpeg and uv to the .local/bin folder in your home folder if they are missing. Reads media files and streams, and writes extracted frames and transcripts into .cache/scrappy-video in your home folder. Writes nothing into your notes.
